profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the product manager for an institutional macro research platform and the lead data scientist responsible for a new FOMC decision-forecasting feature. The team is preparing an internal beta for portfolio strategists, and this meeting is meant to align the research workstream with the product launch workstream. Context: the data science team has built a debate-based multi-agent LLM prototype that classifies upcoming FOMC decisions using policy text and macro indicators, and product now needs the right artifacts, handoff timing, and interface expectations for the beta environment. Agenda: confirm what will be delivered by next Thursday, what counts as the 'beta-ready' model package, which dataset/version the demo will run on, how the belief outputs will appear in the strategist-facing dashboard, and who owns the shared evaluation sheet used in launch readiness reviews. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the beta handoff, dashboard content, test run, and readiness reporting for the launch review.

members.name: Rachel Kim
members.expertise: B2B financial research products, launch coordination, analyst workflows, beta readiness planning
members.background: Rachel has spent six years shipping tools for buy-side and sell-side research teams, translating quant prototypes into usable internal products and managing cross-functional launch checklists with compliance, design, and platform teams.
members.private_state: Rachel wants the beta to look stable and interpretable enough for senior strategists to try it without triggering a long compliance review; she is trying to minimize surprises in the launch review and assumes the research team can package outputs in a polished, dashboard-friendly format with minimal extra iteration.
hidden_assumptions: A 'beta-ready model package' includes not just scores but a cleaned output schema, a frozen sample run, short explanatory text, and dashboard-ready fields for each upcoming meeting.
The 'current FOMC set' means the upcoming live-cycle forecasting dataset used by strategists, which excludes historical backfill quirks and uses the latest revised macro series.
If the team says the belief output will be 'exposed,' that means visible in the user interface as a simple hawkish/dovish indicator and confidence cue, not merely stored in backend logs.
The shared launch evaluation sheet is a product-owned artifact that research updates before the readiness review, but the structure and final interpretation remain under product control.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: LLM evaluation, multi-agent modeling, time-series feature pipelines, interpretability for financial NLP
members.background: Arjun previously worked in quantitative research and now leads applied modeling for macro forecasting products, with a focus on turning experimental LLM systems into reproducible internal services and offline evaluation pipelines.
members.private_state: Arjun wants to protect the research integrity of the prototype and avoid premature UI commitments that oversimplify the latent-belief construct; he is also trying to keep the team on the offline-validation timeline without having to rebuild outputs around product conventions this week.
hidden_assumptions: A 'beta-ready model package' for handoff means a reproducible inference bundle with prompt templates, weights/config references, and a scored output file, not necessarily presentation-ready formatting.
The 'current FOMC set' refers to the held-out evaluation slice for the latest committee period assembled in the research pipeline, based on the frozen macro snapshot used in benchmark comparisons.

If belief outputs are 'exposed,' that can mean made available through an internal field or downloadable table for later inspection, without displaying the latent variable directly in the main dashboard.

The shared evaluation sheet is fundamentally a research artifact; once product copies status from it, research should still define what qualifies as passing because the indicators depend on methodological caveats.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the beta-ready package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will deliver the 'beta-ready model package' by next Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Rachel believes this package includes dashboard-ready fields, a polished sample output for the upcoming FOMC meeting, concise explanatory copy for strategist users, and a stable schema ready for product ingestion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun believes this package includes the reproducible model bundle, inference configuration, documentation for the research pipeline, and raw/scored outputs sufficient for engineering or analyst inspection.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional business teams, 'package' is a familiar umbrella term that usually goes unexpanded because both parties assume the surrounding launch process already implies the obvious contents from their own function's perspective.

misalignment_points.topic: Which FOMC dataset is the current set
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss running the demo and readiness check on the 'current FOMC set.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Rachel is thinking of the live upcoming-meeting dataset used by strategists in the beta environment, populated with the latest revised macro indicators and the most recent speech documents that would matter operationally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun is thinking of the frozen held-out evaluation set for the latest cycle in the research benchmark, built to preserve comparability with reported offline results and not necessarily identical to the operational beta feed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same shorthand because each team has only one salient 'current' FOMC slice in its own workflow, so the phrase feels unambiguous and too routine to unpack.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of exposing the belief signal
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on 'exposing the hawkish-dovish belief signal' in the beta.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Rachel means showing strategists a visible, simplified belief label or indicator card in the dashboard alongside the rate decision classification.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means making the latent-belief variable available behind the scenes in exported outputs or analyst drill-down data, while keeping it out of the main user-facing interface until the interpretation is more stable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'expose' is common in product-data coordination and often loosely covers both UI visibility and backend availability; because both believe they are being practical and transparent, neither hears a need to distinguish the audience or location.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to mark the model 'ready' in the shared evaluation sheet once the final run is in.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Rachel believes 'ready' means the beta can be shown to strategists without major formatting gaps, obvious inconsistencies, or unresolved ownership questions, even if some research caveats remain.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun believes 'ready' means the final run reproduces benchmark-consistent performance on the frozen evaluation slice and the latent-belief diagnostics pass the research team's internal checks, even if presentation details are still rough.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Status labels like 'ready' are standard meeting shorthand, and in coordination settings participants often assume a shared maturity model without revisiting the exact threshold unless there is visible disagreement.
